column1: # Known pre-existing failures. Columns: suite <TAB> failing_assertions.
# THIS FILE IS EMPTY, AND SHOULD STAY EMPTY.
# It used to record 24 accepted failures across 6 suites. That was a mistake, and an
# expensive one: the entries were seven weeks stale, so a full run reported 85
# PRE-EXISTING failures as "net-new" and very nearly buried the 13 that a release
# programme had genuinely introduced. A baseline of accepted failures does not make a
# suite trustworthy — it makes it quiet.
# Every assertion that was failing has since been resolved. Each was verified against
# live product behaviour first, and each turned out to be one of:
#   - a stale expectation (the product had deliberately changed; the test had not)
#   - an environment assumption (a Yoast-only fixture on a Rank Math site)
#   - a fixture that could never match (an AWS key of the wrong length)
#   - or, in four cases, a real bug in the product, which was fixed.
# A regression test must only fail when the product actually regresses. If a suite starts
# failing, fix the product or fix the assertion — do not add a line here.
